info.name: Shipyard Report API
info.description:
Read-only JSON API for the Daily Report Shipyard data. It only returns data — it can't change anything.

## Get started
1. Import this collection (and, optionally, the environment file).
2. Put your key in the **`apiKey`** variable (collection variable, or the environment's `apiKey`).
3. Run **Who am I?** — it should return 200 with your schemas.
4. Run **List tables in a schema**, then read any table.

## Keys
Send the key in the `x-api-key` header (already set on every request). A key is either **permanent** or **expiring** (starts with `srt_`); expiring keys stop working at the time shown by *Who am I?* and the API then answers `401 This API key has expired`.

## Errors
| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | bad `limit`, `offset` or `updated_since` |
| 401 | missing, wrong, expired or revoked key (the message says which) |
| 404 | unknown schema or table — also returned for a schema your key isn't allowed |
| 405 | anything other than GET |
| 500 | server problem; try again, then contact the administrator |

Base URL: `https://mgxdvnnvruoyhnzgrtur.supabase.co/functions/v1/shipyard-report`

item.name: 2. Read a table
item.description: Fetch one table's rows. Page through with `offset` until `next_offset` is `null`.

query.description: Where to start. 0 or more, default 0.

request.description:
Returns up to `limit` rows ordered by `id`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | rows matching the filters |
| `returned` | rows in this response |
| `next_offset` | pass as `offset` for the next page, `null` on the last page |

`numeric` columns (prices) are returned as text so no precision is lost. Ids are numbers. Soft-deleted rows are hidden unless `include_deleted=true`.

item.name: Only rows created or changed since

request.description:
For syncing: returns only rows created or changed after the given time (ISO 8601, e.g. `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`). A row that was never edited counts by its `created_at`.

A table with neither `updated_at` nor `created_at` can't be filtered this way (400).

query.description: Also return rows whose deleted_at is set.

request.description: Most tables mark removed rows with `deleted_at` instead of deleting them, and the API hides those by default. Add `include_deleted=true` to get them too (check `deleted_at` in each row).
